title: Parity P1.3 hipEngine C1 prefill serving-path attribution

host.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S

headline: The C1 prefill deficit is NOT serving-stack overhead: the per-request wall equals the isolated packed-prefill wall, and that wall is GPU-bound in the small-row Q4/Q5/Q6 T16 wmma prefill GEMM family.

server_c1_request_wall_ms.note: warmup 2 arms/width then 10 prompts x 2 arms, Starlette TestClient

isolated_forced_bulk_prefill_s.method: scripts/qwen35_gguf_bench.py --force-bulk-prefill --bulk-prefill-attention-mode bulk --use-wmma-prefill --use-gemv-decode --persistent-session (1 warmup + 3 measured; identical at GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1 and 2)

auto_route_no_selectors_s.note: qwen35_gguf_bench without --force-bulk-prefill falls to a serial per-row path; not the serving route.

route_overhead_packed_vs_bulk_ms.note: packed-AR multi-prompt route vs single-session forced-bulk owners

measured_pass.conclusion: GPU-bound: gaps are ~26 ms; per-launch CPU overhead is not the wall at C1.

kernel_trace.interpretation: The Q4T16 dense wmma prefill family holds 360.6 ms at M=45 rows, ~20x the bandwidth-ideal for its weight traffic (single full weight sweep of 17.1 GB is ~67 ms at 256 GB/s for the WHOLE model; this one family alone exceeds 5x that). The wmma tiling is tuned for large row slabs; at M<=64 it underutilizes the 72-CU device (too few workgroups / latency-bound).

host_profile.method: cProfile (whole bench) + py-spy dump/record (250 Hz, nonblocking)
findings: Engine-thread chain per request: tick -> _run_prefill (525 ms) -> prefill_batch_native -> sampler readback device_synchronize; _run_ar_decode ~50 ms; reclaim/events ~49 ms each.
py-spy: 14.8% of all samples in device_synchronize under _run_prefill, issued by _read_target_block_row_tokens (full-device sync then 4-byte readback).
Serving stack (TestClient + anyio portal + scheduler) adds ~0-30 ms/request; it is NOT the C1 prefill wall.

Startup (one-time, not per-request): eager_load_model -> _speculative_mtp_capability -> resolve_speculative_mtp_serving_plan re-hashes the 17.1 GB model artifact (model_artifact_identity), ~8-10 s; worth caching but parity-neutral.

model_notebook_correction.claim: Campaign doc §2 previously cited 'hipEngine isolated gfx1151 prefill ~1294 tok/s @512 (LCP tranche)' as context.
model_notebook_correction.correction: That published row is Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M (3B-active MoE; benchmarks/results/2026-07-15-gfx1151-gguf-production-refresh-512-64k-128k-blocked.json provenance), NOT Qwen3.8-27B. On the parity model the current-head isolated bulk prefill is 402 tok/s @512. No regression: the numbers were never the same model.

decomposition_c1_prefill_request_ms.gap_to_close: ~300 ms: (a) small-row T16 wmma GEMM efficiency ~230 ms, (b) route overhead ~110 ms

p2_implications: P2.1/P2.2 become: route small slabs to the best owner (kill the ~111 ms packed-vs-bulk overhead) AND fix small-M T16 wmma prefill GEMM efficiency (360.6 -> target <=130 ms at M=45).
P2.3 kernel work is now FIRST-PRIORITY (the wall is below the serving boundary and is a kernel-shape problem), not conditional.

Candidate approaches for the small-M family: N-split/split-K workgroup partitioning to fill 72 CUs at M<=64, low-M tiling variants, or gemv-class batched dispatch; all require strict/production gates per docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md.
C2-C8 rows improve automatically as slab rows grow (W x prompt_len); the small-M fix also lifts the C1 decode-adjacent shapes.
